extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and examiners preparing or reviewing USPTO appeal briefs (appellants, patent attorneys/agents, examiners)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting and reviewing ex parte appeal briefs under 37 CFR 1.192 for the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences (now PTAB), specifying required brief sections, content of arguments for common statutory grounds, procedural requirements, and examiner/board handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of Invention (37 CFR 1.192(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise explanation of the invention defined in the claims involved in the appeal that refers to the specification by page and line number, and, if there is a drawing, to the drawing by reference characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where applicable, it is preferable to read the appealed claims on the specification and any drawing. Referencing page and line numbers may require more detail than a simple summary but is important to enable the Board to quickly determine where the claimed subject matter is described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of the Issues Presented for Review (37 CFR 1.192(c)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise statement of the issues presented for review; each stated issue should correspond to a separate ground of rejection appellant wishes the Board to review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement must include the basis of each issue (e.g., 'Whether claims 1 and 2 are unpatentable under 35 U.S.C. 103 over Smith in view of Jones'), not merely 'Whether claims 1 and 2 are unpatentable.' The statement should be limited to the issues and should not include argument on the merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping of Claims; Separate Patentability Statement (37 CFR 1.192(c)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each ground of rejection that applies to a group of two or more claims, appellant must state whether the claims 'stand or fall together' or state they do not and provide reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant considers claims in a group to be separately patentable, 37 CFR 1.192(c)(7) requires (A) a statement that the claims do not stand or fall together and (B) presentation of reasons why the claims are separately patentable in the argument section (37 CFR 1.192(c)(8)). Merely pointing out differences in claim scope is not sufficient. Absence of the statement and reasons is a concession that the ground, if sustained as to one claim, applies to all; the Board will normally select the broadest claim in the group for decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument Section General Requirement (37 CFR 1.192(c)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellant's contentions with respect to each of the issues presented and the basis for those contentions, including citations of authorities, statutes, and parts of the record relied on, must be presented in the Argument section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All arguments and authorities the appellant wishes the Board to consider should be included in the brief; arguments not included will be refused consideration unless good cause is shown. A supplemental paper may be filed if new authority becomes available after filing (e.g., a pertinent decision published after the brief was filed). Arguments raised for the first time at oral hearing are not normally entitled to consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument Content for 35 U.S.C. 112, First Paragraph (enablement/written description/best mode)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, the brief must contain an argument specifying the errors in the rejection and how the first paragraph of 35 U.S.C. 112 is complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument should address: (a) description of the subject matter defined by each rejected claim; (b) how a person skilled in the art can make and use the claimed subject matter (enablement); and (c) the best mode contemplated by the inventor, where applicable. Use specifics from the specification and drawings as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument Content for 35 U.S.C. 112, Second Paragraph (definiteness)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, the brief must contain an argument specifying the errors in the rejection and how the claims particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide claim-specific explanation identifying why the examiner's assertion of lack of definiteness is erroneous and how each claim limitation is adequately claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument Content for 35 U.S.C. 102 Rejections (anticipation)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102, the brief must specify the errors in the rejection and why the rejected claims are patentable under 35 U.S.C. 102.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include any specific claim limitations that are not described in the prior art relied upon in the rejection and explain clearly how those limitations are absent from the cited reference(s). Identify the claim(s) for which no argument was specified when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument Content for 35 U.S.C. 103 Rejections (obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103, the brief must specify the errors in the rejection and, if appropriate, the specific limitations in the rejected claims not described in the prior art, and an explanation how such limitations render the claimed subject matter unobvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the rejection is based on a combination of references, explain why the references, taken as a whole, do not suggest the claimed subject matter and, as appropriate, why features disclosed in one reference may not be properly combined with another. A general statement that all limitations are not described in a single reference is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument Content for Other Rejections (37 CFR 1.192(c)(8)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: For any rejection not falling under the 112/102/103 subparagraphs, the argument should specify particular claim limitations, if appropriate, or other reasons which cause the rejection to be in error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, for a 35 U.S.C. 101 rejection (nonstatutory subject matter) it may be unnecessary to specify particular claim limitations; instead explain why the claims are statutory (see Ex parte Hibberd example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix Content and Format (37 CFR 1.192(c)(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: An appendix containing a copy of the claims involved in the appeal is required; the copy should be a clean copy and should not include any brackets or underlining as required by 37 CFR 1.121(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For convenience, the copy of the claims should be double spaced and the appendix should start on a new page. See MPEP § 1454 for presentation of claims in a reissue application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include All Required Items and Use Proper Headings/Order (37 CFR 1.192(c) minimums)
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief is in compliance as long as it includes items (1) to (9) in the order set forth (with the appendix at the end), and items should appear under appropriate headings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.192(c) specifies minimum requirements and does not prohibit inclusion of additional material (e.g., list of references, table of contents). Missing section headings or incorrect order is a defect (see form paragraphs for notice of non-compliance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Status of Claims and Identification of Appealed Claims (37 CFR 1.192(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief must contain a statement of the status of all the claims, pending or canceled, and identify the claims appealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to include the claim status and identify appealed claims is a defect and should be specifically indicated in the examiner's notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Status of Amendments Filed After Final Rejection (37 CFR 1.192(c)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief must contain a statement as to the status of any amendment filed subsequent to the final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This informs the Board and examiner how post-final amendments are to be treated for appeal; omission is a defect (see ¶ 12.72).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature, Copies, and Fee Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal brief must be properly signed, submitted in the required number of copies (three copies required under 37 CFR 1.192(a)), and accompanied by the required filing fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsigned briefs, lacking required copies, or unpaid filing fee are defective and may lead to dismissal unless corrected within the allowed periods. See form paragraphs ¶12.12 (unsigned), ¶12.13 (three copies lacking), ¶12.08-12.11 (fee unpaid/dismissal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time Limits for Correcting Noncompliance (37 CFR 1.192(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a brief does not comply with 37 CFR 1.192(c), the examiner will notify the appellant of reasons for noncompliance and appellant will be given the longest of specified time periods to correct defects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time periods are (A) 1 month or 30 days from mailing of notification (whichever is longer); (B) within the time period for reply to the action from which appeal was taken; or (C) within 2 months from the date of the notice of appeal under 37 CFR 1.191. Extensions may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136(a) or (b). Failure to timely file an amended brief that overcomes defects will result in dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: All Arguments/Authorities Must Be Presented in Brief (37 CFR 1.192(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any argument or authorities not included in the brief will be refused consideration by the Board unless good cause is shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments first made at oral hearing are normally not entitled to consideration. A supplemental paper may be filed only if new authority becomes available after filing (e.g., a newly published court decision).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry and Treatment of Amendments and New Evidence After Final Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed after final rejection but before jurisdiction passes to the Board may be entered if it conforms to 37 CFR 1.116; new affidavits or evidence are governed by 37 CFR 1.195; entry is not a matter of right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments requiring a new search, raising new matter, presenting additional claims without cancelling corresponding rejected claims, or introducing new issues will not be entered. New amendments/new evidence must be submitted in a separate paper. Examiners must respond to non-entered amendments and indicate the status of each claim of record or proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's Answer Requirements and Timing (37 CFR 1.193)
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary examiner may furnish a written answer including necessary explanation of the invention, references, and grounds of rejection; the examiner should furnish the answer within 2 months after receipt of the brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The answer should contain a response to allegations/arguments in the brief, call attention to errors in appellant's copy of the claims, and clearly state any withdrawn rejections. The answer must not include a new ground of rejection (unless prosecution is reopened). Examiners should treat affidavits/declarations/exhibits filed with or after the notice of appeal in accordance with 37 CFR 1.195; if such evidence was refused entry, the examiner should not comment on it in the answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: No New Ground of Rejection in Examiner's Answer
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner's answer must not include a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a new ground of rejection is necessary, prosecution must be reopened. The examiner must obtain supervisory approval prior to reopening prosecution after an appeal. Exceptions: if an amendment under 1.116 was entered for appeal purposes and appellant was advised how rejections would apply, the examiner's answer may include those rejections for the added/amended claims as previously advised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply Briefs and Reopening Prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant may file a reply brief to an examiner's answer within two months; the primary examiner must acknowledge receipt and entry of the reply brief or withdraw the final rejection and reopen prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prosecution is reopened, appellant must either (i) file the appropriate reply under 1.111 (non-final) or 1.113 (final), or (ii) request reinstatement of the appeal accompanied by a supplemental appeal brief; no new amendments, affidavits (1.130-1.132), or other evidence are permitted with a reinstatement request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by Reference in Examiner's Answer
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may incorporate in the answer their statement of grounds of rejection by reference to the final rejection or a single other action on which it is based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only statements of grounds of rejection appearing in a single prior action may be incorporated by reference; the answer should not refer to more than one prior action. If statements appear in more than one prior action, they should be quoted and the page/paragraph of the action to be incorporated should be explicitly identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner Should Reevaluate Position and Withdraw Non-Adhered Rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should reevaluate his or her position in light of arguments presented in the brief and expressly withdraw any rejections not adhered to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if a rejection is not repeated in the answer it may be treated by the Board as withdrawn. The answer should include rebuttal of appellant arguments where necessary and avoid confusion from shifting examiner positions without clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal Conference and Group Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Appealed cases may be reviewed by conference in the examining group; the Group Director has discretion on whether to hold conferences and who attends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants may include the primary examiner, the examiner preparing the answer, and a conferee examiner. If a conference is held, the conferee should initial the answer (e.g., 'ABC (conf.)'). If the examiner charged with preparing the answer concludes the appeal should not be forwarded and the primary examiner approves, no conference is held.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of Failing To Address Grounds or To Comply with 1.192(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the brief fails to address grounds of rejection or comply with 37 CFR 1.192(c), the examiner should notify appellant of noncompliance and follow the procedures set forth (allow time to correct, or dismissal if not corrected).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the brief neither states that claims do not stand or fall together nor presents reasons, use the appropriate form paragraph indicating concession. Failure to timely correct defects may result in dismissal and abandonment; limited time extensions may be available under 1.136.
